messages:
maria: Heads-up — my feature branch (feature/prefetch-opt) started failing the integration suite right after I rebased onto main. CI run: https://ci.redwood.com/ci/982321/job/integ-linux. Failing in test_router large payload, looks like an OOM on the runner. Repro locally intermittently. cc @sam @ajay

ajay: Can you paste the failing snippet and the exact test name / job id? Which test is blowing up?

maria: Job 982321, task integration/runner-3. Test: tests/integration/test_router.py::TestRouter::test_large_payload. Log snippet from the CI job:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.1 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 12.8 GiB already allocated)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../tests/integration/test_router.py", line 142, in test_large_payload
    resp = runner.send(payload)
```

sam: That started right after your rebase? Any model/quant/infra changes in your branch, or just main's merge pulling something in?

maria: I only pulled main. Main added a batching config tweak and a new kernel selection change last week — I didn't touch model weights. Locally it passes 3/5 runs; CI consistently fails on the small GPU instance.

ci-bot: integration runner info: runner-3 uses gpu-type=nvidia-t4-small (16GB), image=redwood/integ:2026-02-12

ajay: Two quick checks: 1) try rerunning with REDWOOD_MAX_BATCH=1 to force small batches; 2) try GREATER_GPU for a one-off to see if it's capacity related. If flaky, we should bisect the main merge commits that touched batching/runtime.

maria: Triggered a rerun (982321-rerun-1) and started a local bisect: `git bisect start; git bisect good main~5; git bisect bad HEAD`. Will update if I find the culprit but gotta hop into a client call in ~10m.

sam: If it's likely the new kernel selector, try `REDWOOD_BATCHING_STRATEGY=legacy` in CI to force the old path — that would be a quick canary.

maria: Rerun finished and still failed with the same OOM. Local quick test with legacy batching reduced memory use but wasn't a definitive pass. Bisect paused because one of the intermediate commits needs a build step I don't have set up. @ajay can you take over bisect + CI-assisted runs? I don't have cycles right now.

ajay: Taking this. I'll run a git bisect over the last ~20 commits and request CI jobs for the bisect points (devops, can you spin medium instances for these jobs?). I'll also try the legacy batching env locally to confirm. Assigning to self in the thread.

devops: Provisioned a medium (nvidia-t4-medium) fleet for ajay's bisect jobs and enabled an env toggle so CI runs can use REDWOOD_BATCHING_STRATEGY=legacy or auto. Let me know the job refs and I'll kick them.

sam: Thanks — if bisect shows it's the kernel selector, we'll need a rollback or a hotfix to the selection heuristics. @maria, as a temporary stopgap please add a skip guard to the test (skip if small GPU) so main isn't red for other folks.

maria: Added a tiny guard in my branch and pushed a patch with a note in the PR description. Will remove once we have a root cause. :thumbsup:
